module_summary: cuesupport.cpp is the Ember (PS1 .cue) side of the PS1 library: EMBER/games folder scan, discs.txt manifest parsing, Ember argument validation, settings.txt key:value rewrite, and the merge of POPSTARTER VCD rows with Ember rows (ps1FillGameList, ps1DropTwins). discsupport.cpp (RA editions only) identifies a physical disc, hashes it on the IO worker and launches it with RA telemetry. ethsupport.cpp/.h own the SMB/NFS game page: driver choice (smbman_ra, smb2man, nfsman), logon/open-share, live reconnect and checked refresh on the IO worker, the share picker, the ISO/PS1 backing lists, and the OPL-core and Neutrino launch legs that patch the embedded cdvdman/mcemu IRX settings. favsupport.h declares the favourites/recents store and its on-disk record layout.

reusable_helpers.name: cueSep
reusable_helpers.what: path separator for a device prefix: backslash when the prefix ends in one (SMB), else slash

reusable_helpers.name: cueResolveEmberFile
reusable_helpers.what: compose prefix+folder+sep+file and probe existence with open/close

reusable_helpers.name: cueWriteAll
reusable_helpers.what: write() loop that retries short writes and fails on <= 0

reusable_helpers.name: cueRewriteSettings
reusable_helpers.what: rewrites a key:value text buffer, dropping managed keys and appending the wanted values

reusable_helpers.name: cueRewriteSettingsFile
reusable_helpers.what: read-modify-write of a small text settings file; skips the write when unchanged, restores the original on a failed write

reusable_helpers.name: ps1TwinKey
reusable_helpers.what: strips a POPSTARTER XX./SB./EL./SM. prefix and a leading disc ID from a PS1 title

reusable_helpers.name: smbOpenShare
reusable_helpers.what: SMB open-share with async poll on smb2man and blocking fallback

findings.title: EthSource::update share picker: 64 KB ShareEntry_t sharelist[128] on the IO worker stack is a SIF DMA target with no cache maintenance
findings.problem: The share picker passes a stack array (128 x 512 B = 64 KB of the IO worker's 96 KB stack) as EE_addr; the shipped smbman_ra copies each entry into it with sceSifSetDma (smb_fio.c:1000, DMA_sendEE). Nothing writes back or invalidates the EE data cache for that range and the array is not 64-byte aligned, so a dirty or stale line from earlier deep stack use can override the DMA'd share names that are then read at 847-849.
findings.fix: Align the array to 64 bytes and write back/invalidate its range (SifWriteBackDCache, the pattern fileXioRead uses for its receive buffer) before the GETSHARELIST devctl. Optionally lower maxent (only the 31-char name is kept) to give back most of the 64 KB of worker stack.
findings.justification: Adds one cache-maintenance call and an alignment attribute: the IOP writes this buffer by DMA behind the EE cache, which is a correctness hole on real hardware; one line is the smallest way to make the read coherent.
findings.benefit: Removes a non-coherent DMA read on the share-picker path; with maxent 32 the frame drops from 64 KB to 16 KB of the 96 KB worker stack (INFERRED: sizeof(ShareEntry_t) = 512 per tests/smb2-live/inc-sdk/ps2smb.h:79-83).
findings.evidence: Read ethsupport.cpp:829-866; update() runs on the IO worker via menuDeferredUpdate (opl.cpp:855-871, handler registered opl.cpp:1691); worker stack 96 KB (ioman.cpp:42-44). ps2.yaml:146-154 + :652 show smbman_ra is the embedded smbman; its GETSHARELIST sends entries with DMA_sendEE -> sceSifSetDma (smb_fio.c:871-889, 999-1000). smb2man returns -ENOTSUP (smb2man.c:1708-1710). ShareEntry_t size taken from the in-repo SDK header copy. That fileXioDevctl does no cache op on pointers inside arg is INFERRED (ps2sdk source not in repo). git history: the stack array is inherited from upstream OPL (git show 31e9b1f4^:src/ethsupport.c line 472).

findings.title: EthSupport::reconnectSmb clears the coalescing flags at its end, so a settings reconnect requested while it runs is dropped
findings.problem: requestReconnect (GUI thread, Network page OK) only sets reconnectRequested_ when reconnectQueued_ is 1 (692-696). reconnectQueued_ stays 1 for the whole reconnectSmb run on the IO worker (DHCP/link waits, logon, open-share poll of up to 90 s) and lines 628-629 then clear both flags, so a second OK pressed with corrected settings during that run never reconnects with them.
findings.fix: Move the two clears (628-629) to the top of reconnectSmb, before it reads any settings, so a request that arrives during the run queues a fresh reconnect.
findings.benefit: Fixes a lost settings apply (session stays on the old IP/share until another manual Reconnect); 0 lines, the two assignments move.
findings.evidence: Read ethsupport.cpp:601-709. Callers: grep ethRequestReconnect -> ethsupport.cpp:725 (init) and guisettings.cpp:1056 (Network page exit/OK, no wait on the worker). reconnectSmb runs via IO_CUSTOM_SIMPLEACTION (705); it calls loadModules/initSmb -> netApplyConfig (link/DHCP waitValidState up to ~30 s, netsupport.cpp:68-89) and smbConnect -> smbOpenShare (poll up to 900 x 100 ms, ethsupport.cpp:67-73). That the user can reopen and apply the Network page while the worker is blocked in those RPC waits is inferred from the non-blocking request path, not tested.

findings.title: Share picker in EthSource::update treats ERROR_ETH_LINK_FAIL/DHCP_FAIL as listable and replaces the link error with a share-list error
findings.problem: With no share name set, update() only skips the GETSHARELIST devctl when gNetworkStartup < ERROR_ETH_SMB_OPENSHARE (303). ERROR_ETH_LINK_FAIL (310) and ERROR_ETH_DHCP_FAIL (311), set by netApplyConfig on a pulled cable or failed DHCP (netsupport.cpp:119-143), pass the gate, the devctl fails on the unconnected driver and 864-865 overwrite the status and message with ERROR_ETH_SMB_LISTSHARES.
findings.fix: Also return early when gNetworkStartup is above ERROR_ETH_SMB_LISTGAMES (the link/DHCP codes), so only the open-share and list errors retry the listing.
findings.benefit: Correct error message and no pointless SMB RPC after a link or DHCP failure on the share-picker page; one condition changed, 0 lines.
findings.evidence: Enum values read at iosupport.h:41-60 (CONN 300 .. LISTGAMES 305, LINK_FAIL 310, DHCP_FAIL 311). grep ERROR_ETH_LINK_FAIL/DHCP_FAIL: set only in netsupport.cpp:119-143. initSmb (ethsupport.cpp:370-377) returns after that failure with smbman still loaded, and the deferred update then reaches 832. smbman_ra smb_GetShareList (smb_fio.c:959-981) fails without a session. That setError replaces the earlier message is inferred from host.cpp:86 (setErrorMessageWithCode), not traced further.

findings.title: cuePrepareLaunch skips the 256-byte argv pool check for a folder launch, so an over-long Ember argv is refused only after deinit
findings.problem: The pool check (2*strlen(emberElf)+strlen(argument)+3 > 256) runs only after a discs.txt manifest; with no manifest line 313 returns 1 first. Over SMB the ELF path is up to 52 chars (smb0: + 31-char ETH prefix + EMBER/ember.elf), NFS 56, so a folder name of 150-160 chars (allowed by the scan cap ISO_GAME_NAME_MAX, cuesupport.cpp:502) exceeds the pool; sysLoadELFKeepIOP then refuses after host::app().deinit has already torn the menu down.
findings.fix: Apply the existing pool check on the no-manifest path too (run it before returning 1 at line 313), so the message is shown while the GUI is still live.
findings.justification: The check already exists; it only has to cover the second return path. The concrete problem is a refused handoff after teardown, which leaves the user with no menu.
findings.benefit: Turns a post-teardown launch failure into an on-screen message for long names on network prefixes; about 2 lines moved/added.
findings.evidence: Read cuesupport.cpp:300-344 and the callers' order: ethsupport.cpp:1071 (cuePrepareLaunch) then 1094-1095 (deinit UNMOUNT_EXCEPTION, sysLaunchEmber); same order in bdmlaunch.cpp:88/117, hddsupport.cpp:2211/2230, mmcesupport.cpp:1219/1239, udpfssupport.cpp:850/866. sysLaunchEmber passes argv {emberElf, folder} (system.cpp:1278-1302); pool = strlen(filename)+1 + each argv+1 (elfldr_noreset.cpp:190-205) = 2L+F+3. Lengths: EMBER_FOLDER_DEFAULT/EMBER_ELF_NAME (cuesupport.h:113-114), gETHPrefix[32] (opl.h:501), prefix built at ethsupport.cpp:380-383. What the menu does after a refused handoff post-deinit is inferred, not traced.
